action_taken: Cases of abdominal pain, loose watery stools and vomiting were reported from Village Suk-Manah (Sukumanaha), Sub- District Sarupeta (Pt), District Bajali. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Both children and adults were affected. The affected persons had consumed pre- soaked chana and green mung prepared with coconut and ginger during the Independence Day event at Pallarpar H.S. School. 2 drinking water samples collected were found unsatisfactory on microbiological examination. 1 stool sample collected showed normal gut flora after 24 hours of incubation. Tests were conducted at Barpeta Medical College and Hospital. Medical camps, house-to-house case searches, active surveillance, symptomatic treatment and inspection of food preparation in the premises were conducted. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of loose motion and vomiting were reported from Village Moraj, Sub- District Tarapur, District Anand. District RRT investigated the outbreak. Both children and adults were affected. 3 water samples and 3 stool samples were tested at DPHL, Anand. All 3 water samples were found to be unsatisfactory for drinking, while all 3 stool samples were negative by culture. Of 464 rapid card (RC) tests performed to check proper chlorination, 432 were positive and 32 were negative. Chlorination tablets and ORS sachets were distributed, and pipeline leakages were identified and repaired. Community awareness and health education given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water and food habits, hygiene and sanitation.

Cases of loose motion and vomiting were reported from Village Kalkoti, Sub- District Savanur, District Haveri. District RRT investigated the outbreak. House to house survey was done. Cases were treated at a medical camp established in the locality and at DH Haveri. The probable cause of the outbreak was contaminated water. All cases recovered. Most of the cases were in the age group 16-59 years. 5 stool samples, 4 blood samples, and 4 water samples were collected and sent to IPHL, Haveri. All 5 stool samples were negative for enteric pathogens and Vibrio cholerae by culture. Escherichia coli and Klebsiella spp. were isolated from the 4 water samples. No growth was observed in the 4 blood samples after incubation.Pipeline leakages were repaired by PHED. Chlorination of water sources was done. Community awareness and health education was given by the peripheral team on safe drinking water, hygiene and sanitation.
